<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>The notions <jats:inline-formula id="j_crelle-2014-0136_ineq_9999_w2aab3b7e5510b1b6b1aab1c14b1b1Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mi>𝒲</m:mi>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>{\mathscr{W}}</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>-entropy and reduced volume for Ricci flow were introduced by Perelman, which had proved their importance in the study of Ricci flow. Lei Ni studied the analogous concepts for heat equation on static manifolds, and proved
<jats:inline-formula id="j_crelle-2014-0136_ineq_9998_w2aab3b7e5510b1b6b1aab1c14b1b3Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>

                              <m:mrow>
                                 <m:mi>t</m:mi>
                                 <m:mo>→</m:mo>
                                 <m:mi>∞</m:mi>
                              </m:mrow>
                           </m:msub>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>
                  <jats:inline-formula id="j_crelle-2014-0136_ineq_9997_w2aab3b7e5510b1b6b1aab1c14b1b4Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>

                           <m:mi>𝒲</m:mi>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>\mathscr{W}</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>
                  <jats:inline-formula id="j_crelle-2014-0136_ineq_9996_w2aab3b7e5510b1b6b1aab1c14b1b5Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mo>=</m:mo>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>=</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> ln(<jats:inline-formula id="j_crelle-2014-0136_ineq_9995_w2aab3b7e5510b1b6b1aab1c14b1b7Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:msub>
                              <m:mo>lim</m:mo>
                              <m:mrow>

                           </m:msub>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>
                  <jats:inline-formula id="j_crelle-2014-0136_ineq_9994_w2aab3b7e5510b1b6b1aab1c14b1b8Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mover>
                              <m:mi>V</m:mi>
                              <m:mo>¯</m:mo>
                           </m:mover>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>\bar{V}</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>)
which links the large time behavior of these two. Due to the surprising similarity between those concepts in the Ricci flow and the linear heat equation, a natural question whether such an equation holds for the Ricci flow ancient solution was asked by Lei Ni. In this note, we give an alternative proof to Lei Ni’s equation based on a new method. Following the same philosophy of this method, we answer Lei Ni’s question positively for type I κ-solutions of Ricci flow.</jats:p>
title: An equation linking 𝒲-entropy with reduced volume
